{"summary":"Audit complete; no files were modified. Risk matrix and UX guardrails:

CRITICAL — restore: Replaces managed runtime, configuration, installed MSW tools, and SSH material; stops workspaces but ignores stop failures; accepts a missing checksum with only a warning; preserves Keychain tokens even though restored GitHub metadata may authorize them; retains previous files for rollback and leaves VMs stopped (bin/msw:1470-1738). Relative escaping symlinks are not rejected, only absolute symlinks. Hide under Advanced. Require the existing typed RESTORE phrase; require a stronger RESTORE UNVERIFIED phrase when the checksum is absent. Describe a checksum as integrity evidence, not source authenticity. Accept only user-selected trusted archives, prove every VM stopped before mutation, block concurrent actions, and require GitHub re-verification afterward.

CRITICAL — exec: Runs arbitrary argv in /workspace, auto-starts the VM, and can mutate or delete everything visible inside that workspace, including its Docker runtime (bin/msw:356-406,582-587). Hide under Advanced developer controls. Never build a shell string; pass argv exactly. Show workspace, argv, and auto-start impact, then require EXEC <workspace>. Never retry automatically after timeout or disconnect.

HIGH — GitHub setup/verify/remove: These are mutating operations, not passive credential checks. Setup takes hidden tokens, stores them in Keychain, quarantines and stops the workspace before mutation, writes access metadata, restarts to bind the read secret, then attempts a guest push and—when host-write is enabled—creates, verifies, and deletes a real remote test branch. Failure attempts rollback; incomplete rollback keeps the workspace quarantined. Verify repeats the secret rebind/restart and remote branch exercise. Remove revokes host-write metadata first, restarts to remove the guest secret, then deletes both Keychain items; cleanup failure quarantines the workspace (bin/msw:1114-1363). Require explicit workspace/repository review; typed ENABLE HOST WRITE <workspace> for host-write setup, confirmation for read-only setup and verify, and REMOVE GITHUB <workspace> for removal. Warn that verification can leave an msw-permission-test-* branch if remote cleanup fails. Capture tokens only through a secure PTY/hidden field, never argv, environment, logs, analytics, clipboard history, or crash reports.

HIGH — quarantine/lock trust boundary: setup, verify, and remove use a nonblocking per-workspace kernel lock; the lock file can remain after completion and must not itself be interpreted as busy. The inherited verifier retains the lock if its parent dies. Quarantine markers are written before risky credential changes; normal start/restart/exec/push paths fail closed and quarantine attempts to stop and prove the VM stopped (bin/msw:187-327,333-375). However bin/msw-ssh-proxy:27-59 never checks the quarantine marker, so direct SSH can serve an already-running quarantined VM or restart a stopped one when credentials permit. The app must disable all SSH-derived actions while quarantined, but the repository should be hardened before presenting quarantine as a complete security boundary. Show the stored quarantine reason prominently and offer only GitHub repair. Never clear the marker directly.

HIGH — push: Requires host-write metadata and a Keychain write token, normalizes origin to github.com, fetches before prompting, pushes only the current committed branch through a verified bundle, excludes dirty files/tags/other branches, isolates host Git from ambient config/hooks/environment, and uses an exact observed-SHA force-with-lease (bin/msw:900-1102). Preserve the native PUSH confirmation for normal pushes; show owner/repo, path, branch, SHA, mode, and commit list from the same invocation. Force push belongs under Advanced and requires FORCE PUSH <owner/repo> <branch>. Do not expose --yes directly. Failures can be partial: LFS objects upload before the ref; the ref may succeed before the final guest fetch fails. On any post-initiation error, label outcome unknown, query the remote SHA, and never auto-retry.

HIGH — clean: Defaults to all workspaces, auto-starts them, runs docker system prune -af plus builder prune, and --volumes permanently deletes every unused volume (bin/msw:843-865). Never default the UI to all. Require confirmation for ordinary prune, CLEAN ALL for all workspaces, and DELETE VOLUMES <workspace|ALL> for --volumes. Show that unused containers/images/networks/build cache are deleted even without --volumes. Report per-workspace partial completion.

HIGH — host repair: Uses sudo and nontransactionally installs a root launch daemon/script, changes loopback aliases and /etc/hosts, flushes DNS, generates or reuses an unencrypted SSH private key, updates authorized_keys, and rewrites managed SSH configuration (bin/msw:655-781). Hide under Advanced; require REPAIR HOST, show every host-level target, expect a password prompt, and follow with quick/deep checks. A failure must be shown as partial host configuration, not safely rolled back.

HIGH — upgrade/update: upgrade auto-starts targets and performs apt full-upgrade, autoremove, and clean; default target is all and earlier workspaces remain changed if a later one fails. update changes Homebrew metadata globally or runs msb self update, then doctor; Homebrew upgrade failure is explicitly ignored, so success may mean only doctor passed (bin/msw:605-623). Hide under Advanced maintenance. Require confirmation per workspace and UPGRADE ALL for all; show per-workspace progress. For update, record before/after versions and doctor separately and report partial/unchanged when the ignored upgrade failed.

MEDIUM — backup: Creates a cold sparse archive containing runtime state, MSW configuration, GitHub metadata/quarantine state, and the SSH private key, but excludes Keychain tokens. It stops only workspaces that ping as running and tries to restart that set on every exit; restart failures are warnings and can coexist with “backup complete” (bin/msw:1470-1572). Require confirmation explaining interruption and archive sensitivity, destination/free-space review, and exclusive maintenance mode. Track archive creation, checksum creation, and each VM restart independently; “backup succeeded, restart incomplete” is a valid result.

MEDIUM — resize: Passes memory/CPU values directly to msb modify without local format, capacity, or current-state validation (bin/msw:598-603); configured ceilings are in config.sh:22-36. Place in Advanced resources, show current/requested/ceiling and host headroom, validate locally, and require confirmation. Refresh actual values afterward; failure outcome is unknown until re-inspected.

MEDIUM — tunnel: Validates ports, auto-starts the workspace, then holds an SSH local forward from localhost to guest 127.0.0.1; ExitOnForwardFailure confirms binding, not application health (bin/msw:625-633). Keep custom ports under Advanced, but no typed phrase is needed. Show local exposure, workspace/ports/PID/start time, distinguish “forward active” from “service healthy,” and provide an explicit stop action. Treat process disappearance as closed/stale.

READ-ONLY DEFAULT: Ambient status polling must use only non-starting observations: version, status/ps, fixed URL/port calculation, bounded logs, and direct inspect/status/ping equivalents. Do not poll repos, disk, check --deep, shell/Zed/open, tunnel, or any guest command because ensure_running can start a VM. GitHub status is logically read-only but calls Keychain for credential presence and reports only presence plus verification repo—not access mode, configured time, quarantine, secret binding, or last verification (bin/msw:1311-1320); run Keychain checks on demand or cache briefly to avoid background authorization prompts.

STATE MODEL: Represent VM state as running/stopped/missing/starting/stopping/unknown, never map transport or inspect failure to stopped. Attach source and observed-at timestamps to every value and retain last-known values only with a STALE badge. Model quarantine independently as clear/quarantined(reason)/unknown. Model GitHub as metadata access, repository/configured_at, read-key presence, write-key presence, secret-binding state, and last verification separately; a present write token does not override read-only or missing metadata. After restore, mark GitHub authorization stale until verified. Batch operations need per-workspace succeeded/failed/not-run states. Timeouts, lost subprocesses, and failures after an external mutation begins must say outcome unknown and trigger read-only reconciliation, never automatic replay.

CONCURRENCY: Only GitHub setup/verify/remove are serialized, and only per workspace; push, backup/restore, clean, resize, upgrade/update, host repair, tunnels, and exec have no repository-level coordination. Use a single-flight app action per workspace plus a global exclusive lock for backup/restore/update/host repair, disable conflicting controls, and refresh after every action. This cannot exclude external CLI activity, so preflight data must be considered advisory and destructive commands must revalidate at execution time.

Verification was read-only: implementation, helper scripts, documentation, and focused test scenarios were cross-checked; git diff confirmed no changes to the audited files. Project-wide tests, formatters, and linters were not run as requested.","filesChanged":[]}
